v.praise.sound.1.text: Yes. You looked at the whole letter group, not just one letter.

v.praise.sound.2.text: Two letters, one sound. You spotted it.

v.praise.sound.3.text: That sound matches its letters. Your eyes and ears agree.

v.praise.bridge.1.text: You split it between the twin consonants. That is exactly where the break goes.

v.praise.bridge.2.text: You found the vowel sounds first, and the split followed.

v.praise.bridge.3.text: One vowel sound in every part. You built that bridge carefully.

v.praise.sort.1.text: You looked at the vowel and at what comes after it. That decides the type.

v.praise.sort.2.text: Right clan. The ending of the part told you.

v.praise.sort.3.text: You sorted it by how the vowel is held. That is the skill.

v.praise.catch.1.text: You found the tricky part and remembered it.

v.praise.catch.2.text: That word breaks the rule, and you knew exactly where.

v.praise.catch.3.text: You said the letters, then the word. That is how it sticks.

v.praise.word.1.text: You tapped the parts first, then wrote each one. Good plan.

v.praise.word.2.text: Saying the parts made that word easier to write.

v.praise.word.3.text: Every part is in its place. That is how long words get written.

v.praise.story.1.text: You used the patterns you know to read that long word.

v.praise.story.2.text: A tricky word came up and you worked it out part by part.

v.praise.story.3.text: You looked closely at each part, and the sentence made sense.

v.praise.again.text: Let's look at that one again.

v.praise.listen.text: Listen once more, then you try.

v.praise.tricky.text: That one is tricky. Here is how it goes.

v.praise.reveal.text: Look at the one that is glowing.

v.praise.later.text: A slip just means we need a little more practice with that pattern. It will come back.
